items.title: An explicit separation ratio has an exponential floor

source.anchor: Proposition B.7 Eq19 second inequality and Appendix B.2.2 final proof paragraph A2.SS2.SSS2.p6
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. Scalar comparison from Proposition B.7; the authored Lean proof uses two canonical logarithm tangent estimates instead of the source integral estimate.
source.scope: Only the explicit-ratio to exponential comparison; no actual TV first bound or Poisson evaluation.

items.statement: For every natural dimension \(n\ge3\) and real \(\kappa\ge4\), set \(\rho_\kappa=(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)/(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)\). Then \(\frac12e^{-5n/\sqrt{\kappa}}\le\rho_\kappa^n/(2+4n\sqrt{\kappa}/(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^2)\). This is the second scalar inequality of (19); the first inequality from actual TV to the ratio is separate.
assumptions: All square roots, exponentials, powers and divisions are literal real operations. Positivity is proved internally.

obligations.label: Explicit B7 ratio dominates the exponential floor with coefficient 1/2 and exponent constant5

bindings.boundary: Exact scalar second comparison of B.7 Eq19 at natural n>=3 and real kappa>=4, including kappa4.
